topic: NP pre-1990 linear drift — q557 verification of gufm1 centuries-averaged cross-check patch (ISS-2900)
our_argument_summary: WIN-006 verdict remains Std Model Explains: linear pre-1990 NMP drift is non-discriminating (both globe and dome fit the same NOAA slope); the dome’s asserted 0.0466 deg/yr rate is irreproducible from NP.xy under any of three standard angular-to-linear conventions (1.0–5.2 km/yr vs observed 10–15 km/yr), and — as of the verified patch — the detail_verdict_text now also documents that even on the dome’s own 1590–1990 centuries-averaged scale the gufm1+IGRF reconstruction gives ~1.82 km/yr (~0.0164 deg/yr), so the dome runs ~2.8× too fast on its own preferred timescale.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly identifies that NMP drift has historically been near-linear over the 1590–1990 stretch — gufm1+IGRF backs that up. A regression-slope match on NOAA NP.xy is real (raw-text/02-wins.txt:22 PROS-002 anchor; data/wins.json:WIN-006 detail_evidence references NOAA).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A slope match on a non-discriminating observable is not a model test: both core-mantle convection (globe) and ‘aetheric vortex’ (dome) can be regressed against the same NP.xy points. The dome’s asserted 0.0466 deg/yr cannot be reproduced from NP.xy by any standard angular-to-linear convention and is also ~2.8× too fast on its own 1590–1990 centuries-averaged scale (data/wins.json:WIN-006 detail_verdict_text).
